energy loss (J). Adsorptive metrics include average number of moles adsorbed and desorbed
(n avg.), adsorption capacity (AC), adsorption rate (AR), productivity (P), charge efficiency (CE), and energy consumption (EC).

Figure S2 Voltage and CO2 concentration changes (left) and energetics and adsorptive
performance metrics (right) of BPL electrodes soaked in MgBr2. The electrodes maintain
high capacitance and high CO2 sorption capacity without O2 after being charged/discharged
in the presence of O2


Figure S3 SSA experiments with BPL electrodes and 3M MgCl2 electrolyte. Voltage and CO2
concentration changes from 0 to -1V without oxygen (a) and from 0 to -1V (b), -0.2 to -0.8V
(c), 0 to -0.5V (d) with oxygen. SSA experiments at 1.2 V showing large irreversibility in the
presence of 15% CO2/5% O2/80% N2 (e). CV curves at different voltage windows in the presence of 15% CO2/5% O2/80% N2 gas mixture (f).


Figure S4 CO2 capture versus CO2 release comparison with 3M MgCl2 (a) and 3M MgBr2
(b). Each data point represents an average of 3 adsorption-desorption cycle. For all SSA
experiments, only the bottom electrode was soaked in the electrolyte and top electrode was kept dry.
